title: Developing my own game.
author: Mbsaan
selftext: Hello everyone, I have access to fable and lots of free time. I’m just looking for any known direction for gettings off the ground. I’m trying to make a modern version of an old game I like but have Zero experience. Thank you for any advice.

comments.author: Minute-Animator-376
comments.body:
I have complex setup with much more freedom given to AI using claude/codex/antygravity and it now works for me perfectly where I don't run of quota working 24/7. Basically for visual work I prefer to stick to claude and start with it then 1 run of critic in antygravity and 1 run of opus/astra for polish after critic feedback then back to claude for review in fable 5.2 and additional round of opus. Usually things are just perfect.

Opus is aso coordinating codex doing a review of a code - anything that is not visual work goes to codex straight away.

Antygravity I use mostly as a pair of eyes as their models are great for reviewing a whole video what claude could miss in a screenshots and kinda catches much more issues than claude in regards to visual work - somehow 3d modeling is pathetic. For some work in 3d I also use sol 6.2 in many iterations as it is dirt cheap but a ground work must be done in opus/fable first for best results and finish with opus/fable. Astra/Opus tend to do this work quick and cheap but they are also not so creative, ten to finish early before reaching final polish quality and as for design/placement and understanding the asset requirements and how it needs to look to fit the style and place fable is on another level. I guess for a same price you can get similar results in both but with much more guidance and iterations from your side while working with opus. 

I also have multiple local models to give the tools that other models may lack especially related to vision or 3d modelling, but also for audio and other things and those are integrated into the workflows.

replies.author: Mbsaan
replies.body: Thank you, models and audio are already my biggest concern.

comments.author: buniblasters
comments.body: Wait I need to learn this. I have been using one model for everything. Are you manually switching between models depending on the work or is there some way to set it up?

replies.author: Mbsaan
replies.body: Before I set up a project I ask it to break things down based of what it feels is best grouped together and ask it what it feels the tier should be. Then I get hand off notes for each chat and just paste in a new project chat of the level it ask for. It names and does the rest to set up. That’s not to say that can’t become cumbersome as well, so that’s another thing you have to manage, jumping between chats. Funny enough my chats will often argue that something is not their responsibility and the task should go to another chat. I just pass handoffs until one gives in.
